thread:
marco: Heads up — CI deploys started failing intermittently for project phoenix after yesterday's service-account rotation. Getting 403 from the deploy API.

marco: Error snippet: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`

marco: curl example:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploy -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"ref":"main"}'
# response: {"error":"Token not authorized for project phoenix (aud mismatch)"}
```

anya: That's weird — is it every job or sporadic? Any pattern (branch, runner, region)?

marco: Sporadic — about 30% of deploy jobs in us-west-2. Same runner pool. Fails right after a fresh token get, then retry succeeds ~10s later.

devops-bot: token-refresh event: service-account phoenix-ci@redwood.iam -> ephemeral token minted (ttl=60s, aud=redwood-deploy-service).

sam: My guess is audience claim mismatch + ephemeral token reuse / caching race. The deploy endpoint validates aud=="redwood-ci". Looks like the minting flow started issuing aud="redwood-deploy-service" after the rotation.

sara: Can you paste the decoded JWT (header.payload) from a failing request? Mask exp/iat if needed.

marco: pasted one below (masked):```
{
  "iss": "https://sts.example.com/",
  "sub": "serviceAccount:phoenix-ci@redwood.iam",
  "aud": "redwood-deploy-service",
  "exp": 1710000000
}
```

sam: Yep aud is the issue. Old tokens had aud="redwood-ci". Two paths to fix: update the CI runner token request to ask for aud="redwood-ci" or update the deploy service to accept the new audience (short-term).

anya: Why would it be intermittent? Shouldn't the change be consistent?

marco: We think there's a rollout: some runner replicas still using cached client config (old audience), others using the new token broker that defaults to redwood-deploy-service. When a job routes to a replica that expects redwood-ci it rejects. Retries hit the other replica and succeed.

devops-bot: Observability: token-broker instances by hostname: broker-a(14%), broker-b(86%). broker-b recently deployed with new default audience flag.

ops-team: Temporary mitigation: allow both audiences on the deploy service's verification layer. We can add redwood-deploy-service to the allowed audiences list for 24h.

sam: Can we instead patch the broker config to request aud="redwood-ci"? Less blast radius. Who owns the broker? @ops-team

ops-team: ops-team will push broker config rollback to force aud="redwood-ci" for phoenix namespace. Doing canary on broker-b now. ETA 7m.

marco: Repro steps for engineering:
1) From CI runner, mint ephemeral token: `rwctl token mint --sa phoenix-ci --ttl 60 --aud redwood-deploy-service`
2) Call deploy: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploy`
3) Expect 403 if deploy verifier only allows redwood-ci.

anya: Postmortem checklist:
- Fix broker config so default aud aligns with service validators (sara).
- Add canary/feature-flag for audience change (sam).
- Add a contract test: token broker -> deploy verifier aud must match in CI (marco).
- Short-term: allow both audiences on verifier for 24h (ops-team).

sara: Also check cache TTL on verifier. If verifier caches provider metadata (aud allowlist) for long time, nodes might not see immediate updates. Set cache to 30s for this check.

deploy-bot: rollout started: broker-b config rollback -> aud="redwood-ci" (canary 1/3).

marco: After canary, deploys are passing again for the last 15m. Will monitor. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: Follow-up: we'll add a preflight e2e that mints a token and hits deploy on every broker deploy to catch audience drift early.

anya: Assigning owners: broker config PR (ops-team), verifier canary change (sara), e2e preflight (sam).

marco: tagging for support ticket closure once stable.
